# Mondo sync — the register against the ontology

**Generated by `python3 mondo_sync.py`.** `resolve_mondo.py` finds an
identifier once; this checks that it is still true and reports what Mondo
knows that the register does not. Re-run after a Mondo release.

- Mondo release: **2026-09-01** · checked 2026-09-06
- 122 identifiers checked
- 0 dead · 2 scope warnings · 97 import proposals

## Dead join keys

*(none — every identifier in the register is live in this release)*

## Scope warnings — an `also` entry that is not an equivalence

`also` is read as a list of aliases, and `resolve_mondo.py` searches on
it. A term Mondo scopes as broad or narrow names a different-sized
thing. This is the automated form of the near-miss recorded in
gaps.md #43.

- **hearing-loss** — `also: deafness` — Mondo scopes this **hasNarrowSynonym**, not an exact synonym. It names a different-sized thing (see gaps.md #43)
- **lymphatic-filariasis** — `also: elephantiasis` — Mondo scopes this **hasBroadSynonym**, not an exact synonym. It names a different-sized thing (see gaps.md #43)

## Batch import — what Mondo has that the register does not

**Exact synonyms only.** Mondo scopes its synonyms and only
`hasExactSynonym` is an equivalence; importing the rest would put
differently-sized terms into an alias field. Nothing here is written
automatically — adding a synonym also changes what `resolve_mondo.py`
searches on, which is how five identifiers in this register became
reproducible in the first place.

## Label divergence

Reported, never acted on. Some of these are deliberate: Mondo names
several diseases after their sequela rather than their cause.

- **childhood-all** — we call it **childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia**; Mondo's label is **childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia**
- **childhood-pneumonia** — we call it **pneumonia in children under five**; Mondo's label is **pneumonia**
- **cirrhosis** — we call it **cirrhosis**; Mondo's label is **cirrhosis of liver**
- **cml** — we call it **chronic myeloid leukaemia**; Mondo's label is **chronic myeloid leukemia**
- **ebola** — we call it **Ebola virus disease**; Mondo's label is **Ebola hemorrhagic fever**
- **genital-chlamydia** — we call it **genital chlamydia infection**; Mondo's label is **chlamydia trachomatis infectious disease**
- **hearing-loss** — we call it **hearing loss**; Mondo's label is **hearing loss disorder**
- **heds** — we call it **hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome**; Mondo's label is **Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, hypermobility type**
- **hepatitis-b** — we call it **chronic hepatitis B**; Mondo's label is **chronic hepatitis B virus infection**
- **hepatitis-c** — we call it **chronic hepatitis C**; Mondo's label is **chronic hepatitis C virus infection**
- **hiv** — we call it **HIV infection**; Mondo's label is **HIV infectious disease**
- **hpv-infection** — we call it **anogenital HPV infection**; Mondo's label is **anogenital human papillomavirus infection**
- **marburg** — we call it **Marburg virus disease**; Mondo's label is **Marburg hemorrhagic fever**
- **me-cfs** — we call it **myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome**; Mondo's label is **myalgic encephalomeyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome**
- **mrsa** — we call it **MRSA infection**; Mondo's label is **methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus infectious disease**
- **mycoplasma-genitalium** — we call it **Mycoplasma genitalium infection**; Mondo's label is **Mycoplasmoides infection**
- **neonatal-conditions** — we call it **neonatal conditions**; Mondo's label is **perinatal disease**
- **snakebite** — we call it **snakebite envenoming**; Mondo's label is **snakebite envenomation**
- **stroke** — we call it **stroke**; Mondo's label is **stroke disorder**

## Cross-references — the bridge to everything else

This is what resolving `mondo:` actually bought. Each identifier below
is a join key into a dataset the register cannot currently reach.

| source | records | what it unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| `MEDGEN` | 117/122 | NCBI concept hub — links OMIM, Orphanet, GTR and literature |
| `UMLS` | 117/122 | concept mapping across vocabularies |
| `DOID` | 106/122 | disease ontology |
| `NCIT` | 106/122 | cancer and biomedical terminology |
| `SCTID` | 105/122 | clinical coding (SNOMED CT) |
| `MESH` | 97/122 | literature search |
| `ICD9` | 92/122 | burden — historical coding, still the key for older series |
| `icd11.foundation` | 74/122 | burden — current WHO classification |
| `EFO` | 64/122 | experimental factor ontology — the key into GWAS and biobank data |
| `ICD10CM` | 64/122 | burden — the route into GBD cause mappings |
| `GARD` | 54/122 | rare disease information |
| `Orphanet` | 53/122 | RARE DISEASE PREVALENCE — publishes prevalence classes, not point estimates |
| `MedDRA` | 34/122 | adverse event and regulatory coding |
| `ICD10WHO` | 30/122 | burden — the route into GBD cause mappings |
| `NANDO` | 23/122 | Japanese intractable disease designations |
| `OMIM` | 23/122 | genetic — gene and variant level |
| `HP` | 17/122 | — |
| `NORD` | 17/122 | rare disease information |
| `ONCOTREE` | 8/122 | — |
| `birnlex` | 7/122 | neuroscience terminology |
| `ICDO` | 5/122 | oncology morphology coding |
| `OMIMPS` | 3/122 | OMIM phenotypic series |
| `CSP` | 2/122 | — |
| `MFOMD` | 1/122 | mental functioning ontology |

## Sub-entities — the distinctions we make against the ones Mondo holds

### Pointing at a parent — candidates to review

**The record names something narrower than the term it cites.** Every
join made on this identifier silently widens to the parent, which is
how a burden figure for the whole disease ends up attached to a record
about one form of it.

**These are candidates and never fixes, and `--apply` will not touch
them.** The tool cannot tell a narrower term for this entity from a
sibling that merely shares its words — `pleomorphic adenoma of the
salivary gland` returns *carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma*, which is a
malignant transformation and a different disease. Pointing at a broader
term is also sometimes deliberate.

- **pleomorphic-adenoma** — we call it **pleomorphic adenoma of the salivary gland** and point at `MONDO:0008401` **pleomorphic adenoma**, which is BROADER. Mondo also has `MONDO:0006285` **major salivary gland carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma**, `MONDO:0006403` **salivary gland carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma** — **candidate(s) to review, not a fix**: these may be narrower terms for this record, or siblings that merely share its words

### No term exists — the ontology cannot hold this distinction

**This is gaps.md #227.** The record points at its parent because
nothing narrower exists. Filing the term upstream is the fix; until
then the register carries a distinction nobody outside can cite.

- **acute-bronchitis** — **acute bronchitis** has no Mondo term; the record points at the parent `MONDO:0003781` **bronchitis**. The ontology cannot hold a distinction this register makes (gaps.md #227)
- **childhood-pneumonia** — **pneumonia in children under five** has no Mondo term; the record points at the parent `MONDO:0005249` **pneumonia**. The ontology cannot hold a distinction this register makes (gaps.md #227)
- **h-pylori-ulcer** — **peptic ulcer disease caused by Helicobacter pylori** has no Mondo term; the record points at the parent `MONDO:0004247` **peptic ulcer disease**. The ontology cannot hold a distinction this register makes (gaps.md #227)
- **h5n1** — **H5N1 avian influenza** has no Mondo term; the record points at the parent `MONDO:0018695` **avian influenza**. The ontology cannot hold a distinction this register makes (gaps.md #227)
- **influenza** — **seasonal influenza** has no Mondo term; the record points at the parent `MONDO:0005812` **influenza**. The ontology cannot hold a distinction this register makes (gaps.md #227)

### Aliases the ontology holds as entities — candidate sub-records

**NOT a defect list.** `also` is *"synonyms people actually search
for"* (SCHEMA.md), explicitly allowed to be broader or narrower than
the entity, and its only consumer is free-text search. Somebody typing
`pernicious anaemia` should land on the `anaemia` record, and that is
this field working.

What the list is for: these are the aliases Mondo holds as **entities in
their own right**, so each is a candidate for its own record — or for a
stratum — if the register ever decides the parent is doing too much
work. Same question as the strata section, asked from the other side.

### Strata the ontology could address

**Positive findings only, and the silence is not evidence.** A stratum name
is often a descriptive phrase rather than a disease name, so searching one
and finding nothing tells you nothing — reporting that null would be a
check that could not run reporting a result. Absence of a record below
does NOT mean Mondo lacks a term for that stratum.

**And a one-word stratum name can match a qualifier rather than a
disease.** `prion-disease`'s stratum `acquired` matches a Mondo term
literally labelled *acquired*, which is not an entity anyone would cite.
No filter removes it without also removing `dysentery` and `hydrocele`,
which are one word and genuine — so it is left visible and named here.
